fundamental.headline: Solid business, fairly priced
fundamental.health: Sales up 22% over the last year, it keeps 4 cents of every sales dollar as free cash, it has more cash than debt.
fundamental.price_text: You're paying about its usual price: its price vs sales is in the middle of its 5-year range. However, it looks pricier than similar companies once growth is considered.
drivers: It is spending heavily on new capacity (much of it AI), faster than sales are growing; the payoff isn't proven yet.
news: Recent guidance update is bad news for the company (not yet confirmed); the stock hasn't reacted much yet, and it could matter for months.
Recent AI/infrastructure spending news is bad news for the company (not yet confirmed); the stock already reacted, so much of it is likely in the price, and it could matter for months.
fundamental.take: Good business at a fair price: reasonable to own, no urgency to buy. This is research, not personal advice.

deeper.title: What the price assumes
deeper.text: The price assumes about 36% a year growth in free cash flow for 10 years, then 3% (discount rate 9.8% = 10-year Treasury 4.8% + 5%; base: last 12 months of free cash flow). For comparison, sales grew 22% last year; 17%/yr over 3 years — the market expects faster growth than the company has recently delivered.

deeper.title: Return on capital
deeper.text: 24% (3 years ago 40%, falling) — each $100 invested in the business (debt + equity, net of cash) earns about $24 a year after tax; return on shareholders' equity 35% (3 years ago 24%).

deeper.title: Signed future revenue
deeper.text: Signed but not yet delivered (remaining performance obligations): $567.7B, up 260% from a year ago — about 1.2× the last 12 months of sales; customer prepayments not yet earned (deferred revenue): $12.6B, up 70% from a year ago.

deeper.title: Earnings-quality red flags
flags: Profit leans on non-operating gains: net income $235.7B vs operating income $157.0B over the last 12 months (e.g. investment gains or one-offs that may not repeat).

deeper.title: Multi-year view
deeper.text: Sales grew 17%/yr over 3 years and 15%/yr over 5 years; operating margin today 33% vs a 5-year range of 25–33% (median 31%): near the top of a fairly narrow range.
deeper.margin_position: near the top of a fairly narrow range

deeper.title: Cash returned to shareholders
deeper.text: Returned $5.9B to shareholders over the last 12 months ($5.9B buybacks + $0M dividends) = 0.2% of the company's market value. Share count up 1.4% from a year ago (stock pay outpacing buybacks — dilution).

deeper.title: Analyst estimates
deeper.text: Next year's earnings-per-share estimate $14.95, up 1% in 90 days; 16 analysts raised, 23 cut in 30 days. This year's earnings-per-share estimate $19.53, down 5% in 90 days (down 5% in the last 30); 3 analysts raised, 38 cut in 30 days. Source: Yahoo (unofficial).

deeper.title: Vs peers
deeper.text: Compared with 5 peers (META, MSFT, AMZN, NFLX, ORCL): sales growth 22% vs a median of 18%; operating margin 33% vs 32%; price/sales 7.5× vs 5.2×.

deeper.title: Where sales come from
deeper.text: By segment, latest quarter vs a year earlier: Google Services 75% of sales, up 11%; Google Cloud 24% of sales, up 103%; Other Bets 0% of sales, up 8%. Source: 10-Q XBRL.

deeper.title: Insider trading
deeper.text: Last 90 days: no open-market purchases; sales $79k, 100% under pre-set 10b5-1 trading plans. Source: SEC Form 4.

deeper.text: 1 new risk-factor heading vs last year's annual report, e.g. “Disruptions in our ability to access future financing or manage our indebtedness could adversely affect our ab…”.

tiles.title: Earnings per share
tiles.sub: -26% vs a year ago · $19.06 over 12 months (GAAP)
tiles.read: Profit per share fell 26% while sales grew 25%: costs are rising faster than sales.
tiles.explain: EPS = profit divided by the number of shares. The quarterly figures are the 'adjusted' EPS analysts track (Yahoo); the 12-month figure is the official GAAP number from SEC filings.

tiles.title: Earnings vs forecasts
tiles.sub: last 8 reports · bars = EPS beat (+) or miss (−) vs the average forecast
tiles.read: Missed forecasts last quarter by 30%; another miss would suggest the business is weaker than expected.
tiles.explain: A 'beat' means reported EPS came in above the average analyst forecast. Source: Yahoo (unofficial).

tiles.title: Sales growth
tiles.read: Sales up 25% from a year ago, about as fast as two quarters ago (22%): steady demand.
tiles.explain: Growth of quarterly sales (revenue) compared with the same quarter a year earlier.

tiles.title: Profit margins
tiles.read: Each $100 of sales leaves $33 of operating profit, about the same as a year ago.
tiles.explain: Operating margin = operating profit ÷ sales. Gross margin = what's left after the direct cost of the product.

tiles.title: Free cash flow
tiles.read: Just 8% of reported profit became spare cash: much of the profit is tied up in spending or working capital.
tiles.explain: Free cash flow = cash from operations minus spending on equipment and buildings: money the company could return or reinvest.

tiles.title: Price vs profits (P/E)
tiles.read: You pay 15× last year's profit (lower than 96% of the last 5 years; below peers' 21); 18× next year's forecast, so profits are expected to fall.
tiles.explain: P/E = share price ÷ earnings per share. Forward P/E uses next year's forecast earnings.

tiles.title: Company outlook
tiles.read: No numeric outlook was found in the latest earnings release, so the next report carries more surprise risk.
tiles.explain: Guidance = what management says it expects for the next quarter or year, from its 8-K earnings release.

tiles.title: Forecast changes
tiles.read: Next year's EPS forecast is up 1% in 90 days (16 raised, 23 cut lately): forecasts are steady.
tiles.explain: How the average analyst forecast for next year's earnings per share changed (Yahoo, unofficial).
